etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from New Latin tactica, from Ancient Greek τακτικός (taktikós, “fit for ordering”), from τάσσω (tássō, “to order, to arrange”).

definitions.definition: A maneuver, or action calculated to achieve some end.

quote.citation: 2019 September 10, Jonathan Guyer, The American Prospect‎[1], number Fall 2019:
quote.text: Omar has challenged Elliott Abrams’s record in Latin America, taken a firm line against Saudi Arabia and the Emirates, and advocated for—wait for it—the two-state solution for Israel and Palestine (even though the headlines have focused on her expressing support for the right to boycott as a tactic).

definitions.definition: (military) A maneuver used against an enemy.
(chess) A sequence of moves that limits the opponent's options and results in an immediate and tangible advantage, typically in the form of material.
(dated, military) Tactical; of or relating to the art of military and naval tactics.

quote.citation: 1831, Thomas Campbell, The Power of Russia:
quote.text: But time will teach the Russ, ev'n conquering WarHas handmaid arts: aye, aye, the Russ will wooAll sciences that speed Bellona's car,All murder's tactic arts, and win them too  […]

definitions.definition: (chemistry) Describing a polymer whose repeat units are identical
